name: cli-init
body: `kalide init [path] [--local]` in the current directory creates the deck's `slides/`, an empty `assets/` directory for images, and a valid `kalide.yaml`. It accepts an optional external-library `path` argument and the optional `--local` flag; there is no `--force`. It selects the template library per init-library-resolution: an explicit `path`, else the configured user-level default (default-template-dir), else the built-in starter deck. In the built-in starter-deck branch — no path, no configured default, or `--local` — it writes one valid starter slide into `slides/` and creates the project's minimal local `templates/` directory (cli-init-minimal-seed), and refuses if a local `templates/` already exists. In the external-library branch — an explicit `path` or the configured default — it writes `templates: <path>` into `kalide.yaml`, writes an empty `slides/` (the new deck starts with no slides), leaves the local `templates/` untouched (it writes none), and validates the library at `<path>` fail-fast BEFORE writing anything — the pre-write check reads the external library at `<path>` alone and does not read a local `templates/`; a valid library needs only `library.yaml` plus the templates-dir-layout structure and need define no template, but the deck's theme (optional, default `default`) must resolve in it (theme-selection); an invalid or missing library, or a library that does not resolve the deck's theme, aborts with a clear error naming the path, a non-zero exit and nothing written. In the explicit-path case (step 1 of init-library-resolution) a relative path is stored as given (resolved against the deck root); in the configured-default case (step 2) the resolved default is stored as an absolute path (default-template-dir). In the external-library branch a pre-existing local `templates/` does not block init (see cli-init-refuse-existing); init leaves it untouched (never deleted, never overwritten) and it participates as the deck's local library layer that `kalide start` loads (layered-template-library). Because the pre-write check reads the external library alone, a name carried by both the external library and a local layer is not detected at init and surfaces as a duplicate when `kalide start` loads the merged library (library-layer-uniqueness). Both forms also write a project-root `AGENTS.md` — the shared deck-author agent guide (agent-authoring) — verbatim from a static file embedded in internal/scaffold; it is text-only, not a template asset and inert to the deck loader, so `kalide start` is unaffected. The guide is written ONLY when no `AGENTS.md` exists at the target: a pre-existing `AGENTS.md` never blocks init (neither branch) and is left byte-for-byte untouched while the deck is still scaffolded normally. AC: immediately after a seed init (no path and no configured default, or `--local`), `kalide start` validates cleanly and serves the starter slide; after `kalide init ../lib` against a library that resolves the deck's theme (which need define no template), `kalide start` validates and serves the deck from `../lib` (the slide set may be empty); `kalide init ../bad-lib` — invalid library, or a library that does not resolve the deck's theme — fails before writing anything; with a configured default that is a valid library, `kalide init` writes an external-library deck referencing it while `kalide init --local` writes the seed deck; scaffolding into a directory that already holds an `AGENTS.md` succeeds and leaves that file byte-for-byte unchanged, with the scaffolded `AGENTS.md` written only when none exists; scaffolding with `kalide init ../lib` into a directory that already holds a local `templates/` succeeds and leaves that directory untouched, and the local `templates/` loads as the deck's local layer alongside `../lib`, with a name carried by both failing at `kalide start` rather than at init.
